prompt:
Create a Minecraft builder reference sheet, landscape 3:2. Crisp voxel style using vanilla Minecraft blocks only, plain light background, no characters or animals. Two views side by side of the SAME complete site at the SAME scale: LEFT straight-on front elevation, orthographic, viewed from the logging road; RIGHT a three-quarter view showing front, east sides and rear yard. Keep both complete sites and smoke fully in frame. Skilled human builder quality: real massing, projecting details, recessed and framed openings, roof verges, eaves and ridges, block-accurate stairs, slabs, fences, trapdoors, panes and hanging lanterns. No smooth geometry or invented blocks.
Site: northern lumber camp in a cut-over spruce clearing, 40 blocks wide and 34 deep, with a rutted logging road of brown dirt and gravel along the front. On the left a long low 1½-storey bunkhouse of dark bark-on horizontal spruce_log courses on a grey cobblestone plinth; walls 6 blocks high, roof ridge y=14. At corners logs cross and project beyond walls, alternating each course. Its steep grey slate-shingle gable roof runs along the road; dark eaves and pale stripped-spruce boards fill both gable triangles. A covered spruce plank porch runs along the front under a low shed roof on pale posts, simple spruce rail, two hanging lanterns flanking a spruce door. Shuttered square glass windows in log walls. Chunky mossy fieldstone chimney outside the east gable, past ridge, puffing cook smoke. Cordwood under west eave and open woodshed lean-to at back.
To the right, across a dirt path, taller-looking open sawmill pole frame with pale stripped-spruce posts, knee braces and heavy top beam, but the same ridge height y=14. Its 45-degree grey slate gable faces the road, plank gable end, small loft door and spruce_wall_sign reading exactly "SAWMILL". A louvred ridge vent. Dark interior with saw carriage running front to back, represented with vanilla stonecutter, spruce slabs, trapdoors and dark beams. In front a low pyramid of bark-on logs on skids ready to roll in. Against mill east side a red brick boiler stack, dark deepslate band and stepped brick-slab cap, masonry to y=19, sending a tall white smoke column high above camp. Behind mill exactly three stacks of pale fresh-sawn birch boards with dark spacer strips along dirt lanes. Scattered spruce stumps, patchy grass/coarse dirt/podzol, chopping block by back path, tall dark spruce cone trees around lot edges.
Use these exact Minecraft block ids as the allowed palette, grouped by role:
bunkhouse_logs: spruce_log.
plinth_chimney: cobblestone, mossy_cobblestone, stone_bricks, cobblestone_slab, cobblestone_stairs.
pale_timber: stripped_spruce_log, stripped_spruce_wood.
planks: spruce_planks, spruce_slab, spruce_stairs, spruce_fence, spruce_fence_gate, spruce_door, spruce_trapdoor, spruce_wall_sign, spruce_pressure_plate.
glass: glass_pane.
roofs: cobbled_deepslate, cobbled_deepslate_stairs, cobbled_deepslate_slab, deepslate_tiles, deepslate_tile_stairs, deepslate_tile_slab, polished_deepslate, tuff_bricks, tuff_brick_stairs, tuff_brick_slab, stone_brick_stairs, stone_brick_slab, dark_oak_planks, dark_oak_stairs, dark_oak_slab.
brick_stack: bricks, brick_slab, deepslate_bricks.
lumber: birch_planks, birch_slab.
ground: grass_block, coarse_dirt, podzol, rooted_dirt, dirt_path, gravel, short_grass, fern.
trees: spruce_log, spruce_leaves.
Allowed functional/decor blocks: barrel, chest, ladder, red_bed, white_wool, white_carpet, bookshelf, crafting_table, composter, anvil, lectern, campfire, smoker, furnace, blast_furnace, stonecutter, grindstone, cauldron, lantern, iron_chain, hay_block. These are available props, not a requirement to display every one. Use campfire smoke for chimney emissions, with voxel white_wool/white_carpet only if needed for static smoke. Keep details buildable. Label panels "FRONT ELEVATION" and "THREE-QUARTER VIEW"; no palette legend.
changes: Saved the built-in image generation output unchanged as concept.png in the current directory.
Palette roles retain every planned block; added ids are visual interpretations and buildable equivalents, not an exact recoverable block inventory.
Views are stacked vertically: front elevation above, three-quarter view below, instead of side by side.
The front elevation includes visible depth and is not strictly orthographic. Equal scale between views is not verifiable.
The bunkhouse has two added front-facing gables with upper windows rather than only pale triangles at the ends of a single longitudinal gable roof.
The porch covers the central portion of the bunkhouse rather than its full frontage.
Corner log ends repeat vertically; alternating crossed courses are not clearly represented.
The bunkhouse appears to have a double entrance door rather than one spruce door.
The mill loft opening appears as paired shutter panels, and additional lanterns decorate the mill.
The west cordwood shelter is visible, but a separate rear woodshed lean-to is not clearly shown.
The three birch lumber stacks sit prominently east of the mill rather than wholly behind it.
The mill ridge vent appears as a raised ridge structure without clearly resolved louvres.
The saw carriage adds rail-like tracks and metal bars outside the supplied palette; rail and iron_bars are the closest vanilla block equivalents.
Stone post bases imply cobblestone_wall and mossy_cobblestone_wall shapes beyond the supplied palette.
Smooth diagonal knee braces, thin metal fittings, small cordwood rounds and fine board spacers do not consistently match vanilla block geometry.
An axe appears embedded in the chopping stump. It is an item depiction, not a vanilla placeable block.
Smoke is rendered as soft particle-like puffs, with upper plumes clipped by panel boundaries; campfire blocks themselves are not visible.
Exact 40-by-34 dimensions, six-block wall height and y=14/y=19 elevations cannot be confirmed from the picture.
The road has dirt and gravel texture, but distinct wheel ruts are weakly defined.
